articleTitle: Towards the Extension of FPG-AI Toolflow to RNN Deployment on FPGAs for On-board Satellite Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: In recent years, research in the space community has shown a growing interest in the deployment of Deep Neural Networks on-board satellites, mostly driven by system miniaturization and commercial competition. Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) have proven to be competitive accelerators for these algorithms and works proposing methods for automating the design on these devices have acquired relevance. The common purpose is to enable a wide range of users without specific skills to accelerate DNN models on FPGA with reduced development times. This paper describes the process of improving FPG-AI, a novel technology-independent toolflow that efficiently automates DNN deployment on FPGAs belonging to different vendors and with desperate resource budgets. The proposed techniques are meant to be a first step towards the extension of FPG-AI to Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), a subset of DNNs designed for processing sequences of data. As a first step, we discuss model compression strategies for enabling energy-efficient hardware acceleration of Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs), one of the most popular RNN layers. The article then presents a GRU-based hardware accelerator designed to be compliant with the identified quantization algorithm. The architecture features an optimized dataflow to enable hardware reuse over time and maximize resource efficiency without affecting the performance of the architecture. Preliminary results are reported for a state-of-the-art RNN-based model for Fault Detection Isolation and Recovery (FDIR) onboard the satellite to evaluate the proposed methods. A comparative analysis is also performed with the NVIDIA Jetson Nano Embedded GPU to characterize our accelerator with respect to a state-of-the-art platform for RNN inference.

articleTitle: Advanced Data Handling Architecture (ADHA): Status, Current Activities and Industrial Road Map
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: To contribute towards the European Space Agency’s (ESA) objectives of reducing spacecraft development time, achieving cost efficiency, and promoting faster adoption of innovative technologies, the On-Board Computer and Data Handling Systems section (TEC-EDD) is currently engaged in several activities with European industry partners, having the aim to develop across ESA member states an Advanced Data Handling Architecture (ADHA) based on standardized, interchangeable, and inter-operable electronics modules equipped with the latest generation of microelectronics components.This short paper introduces the concept of ADHA, its current status, its benefits and the future perspectives it opens.

articleTitle: Mytikas Demonstrator
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: NG-Ultra with DDR4 for high memory bandwidthWith a radiation-hardened 500k LUT FPGA matrix and a complete quad-core ARM System-on-Chip, NG Ultra offers exceptional processing capabilities for space applications. However, such potential can only be fully experienced in an ecosystem where memory bandwidth is not a limiting factor.Through the Mytikas initiative, Airbus Defence and Space (ADS) in collaboration with NanoXplore (NX) is pioneering the use of DDR4 memories with the NG Ultra component. The project aims to leverage ADS’s experience of similar designs with Xilinx components in order to develop a demonstrator able to demonstrate the ability of NG Ultra to interface DDR4 memory with the necessary margins required in space environments.This presentation will be an opportunity to detail ADS’s chosen architecture, the challenges it has overcome in order to design the demonstrator with a specific emphasis on PCB layout, and also measured performance.

articleTitle: A Modular, Reconfigurable and Portable Framework for On-Board Data Processing: Architecture and Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: A balance between meeting customer data requirements and delivering timely, tailored solutions is critical. The Astral Intelligence Toolbox is a framework that provides a modular, reconfigurable architecture for developing and deploying software applications for on-board processing. Different use cases, processing targets and data sources can be rapidly targeted using a combination of reusable software components and development tools. This allows customer requirements to be quickly mapped to component selection and configuration. Applications can then be iteratively developed from demonstration through to flight. Case studies for configured applications are presented and result shown, based on engagements with end users during an ESA InCubed activity.

articleTitle: OBC-Ultra, the rad-hard NG-Ultra-based On Board Computer for future applications
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: This paper will present the OBC-Ultra, the new generation of On Board Computer developed by Airbus and based on the European rad-hard NG-Ultra.The OBC-Ultra is the new generation of Airbus On Board Computer (OBC) targeting both Telecommunication and Earth Observation missions. It is based on the European rad-hard FPGA & SoC from NanoXplore named the NG-Ultra.This new equipment directly benefits from the Airbus database and experience acquired through several H2020, GSTP and internal R&D projects on NG-Ultra-based applications, from generic VHDL & Low Level Software (SW) libraries to place and route automatisation and optimisation of FPGA designs.This presentation will describe the architecture of this new NG-Ultra-based OBC by presenting the VHDL and low level software modules and by explaining how the use of NanoXplore components allows the attainment of high data rate performances across the different boards while offering a European-based solution critical for our strategic non-dependence:•Wide range of communication protocols (SPW, CAN, 1553, RS485) on NG-Ultra-based processing board•Critical functions (Reconf, Security, ETC, ETM) on Ultra-300-based board without SW•20Mbps TM/TC distributed across 2 boards for both SW performances and HW critical functions independence•Latest Space Data Link Security (SDLS) Extended Procedures standard support•Mass Memory function on processing board with Flash NAND and HW autonomous modules•Advanced HW & SW Debug and Trace features•Carefully considered HW/SW architecture for complex, multicore SW and critical autonomous HW.•Boards respecting modular ADHA standardThis presentation will be an opportunity for Airbus to detail the current development status of OBC-Ultra.

articleTitle: After six months successful operations in low earth orbit: data processing system architecture and lessons learned from the LisR mission
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: The LisR (Longwave Infrared Sensing demonstrator) mission was a successful technology demonstrator mission conducted on the Nanoracks Experimental Platform (NREP) outside the International Space Station (ISS). Launched in February 2022, the mission aimed to monitor the Earth's surface temperature using a cryo-cooled thermal infrared imager. The system components were based on commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) components, following a New Space approach. To ensure the robust operation of the COTS electronics in the Low Earth Orbit (LEO) environment, various protective measures and operational precautions were implemented. During its nearly six months in orbit, with four and a half months of operation and three and a half months of active imaging, the LisR mission achieved significant success. The payload acquired over 9.3 million frames and captured approximately 500 million km2 of land surface, providing a valuable dataset for ongoing and future research. This mission also showcased Fraunhofer EMI's onboard Data Processing unit for small satellites which is also used in in succeeding missions. While LisR had limitations of a rapid new space mission, it also serves as a prime example of how such an approach enables missions with limited budgets and tight schedules to achieve remarkable results.

articleTitle: COTS GPU Processor Development for On-board Demonstration
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: Our COTS GPU processor will be demonstrated on-board with JAXA’s satellite which is planned to be launched in JFY2024. We will try to obtain basic behavioral data in space, and plan to apply the knowledge gained to the system for future missions.

articleTitle: A new concept of Remote Interface Units
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: European space industry, together with the European Space Agency, is promoting the standardization of the data-handling and processing architectures, down to the level of electronic modules. In this context, this paper shows Airbus Crisa’s vision of how the usual electronic modules that form part of a Remote Terminal / Interface Unit (RTU / RIU) might be.

articleTitle: Application of SpaceWire and SpaceFibre in GR765
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: The GR765 is a radiation-hardened system-on-chip planned to be the successor of the GR740 quad-core LEON4FT microprocessor. The GR740 is the highest performing LEON-based processing component currently available for space applications and is being applied in various missions and spacecraft architectures.The GR765 architecture includes several improvements over the GR740, most notably the addition of a bootstrap option to select between the SPARC V8 LEON5FT and the RISC-V NOEL-V FT high-performance processors thereby increasing computational performance over the LEON4FT used in the GR740. The GR765 provides a low-threshold upgrade path for current GR740 users that need additional computational performance, improved power performance, or that would benefit from the extended functionality in the new architecture.This paper provides an overview of the GR765 architecture and then focuses on the application of SpaceWire and High-Speed Serial Links in the GR765 chip. The benefits of using these communication protocols in space applications are discussed, including high-speed data transfer, fault tolerance, and radiation hardening. The design and implementation of the SpaceWire and High-Speed Serial Links interfaces in the GR765 chip are presented in detail. Additionally, the paper describes the planned extensions to the GR765 chip and their potential applications. The schedule and status of the project are also provided.

articleTitle: Development of the CREOLE ASIC and the Next-Generation On-Board Computer
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: The Single Board Computer Core (SBCC) activity was an ESA funded activity initiated with the aim of evolving the previous generation of Beyond Gravity’s on-board computers (OBCs), which were based on a set of ASICs implementing the processing function, mission and data link interfaces, memory controllers, authentication functions, telemetry, telecommand, reconfiguration, on-board time etc. To improve integration, reduce mass, volume, and AIT costs it was decided to integrate all these OBC functions into a single ASIC, which would form the core of a Single Board Computer (SBC) concept, and the subsequent next-generation on-board computer (OBC-NG).This resulting ASIC was codenamed CREOLE. It was developed, verified, manufactured, tested and fully validated within the scope of this activity. It is the core of the single board computer, which was also developed in this activity. Complemented by a power supply module, these modules form the next-generation OBC (OBC-NG) unit, which has already been selected for use in several institutional ESA missions, such as PLATO, CO2M and ARIEL.This paper will provide an overview of the development and architectures of CREOLE, the SBC core, and the rest of the modules comprising the next-generation OBC.

articleTitle: Robust Machine Learning Systems For Dependable Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning have attracted lots of attention to the space engineering community the last few years. In this paper, an attempt to utilize the concept of Machine Learning is presented for a robotic mission to other planets (in this paper is focused on Mars) for planetary exploration purposes. Although, building a machine that is able to learn is not achieved (and it is not yet feasible to be built in general), the borrowed ideas, concepts, and products from the research domain on Machine Learning, provided the necessary engineering tools for improving the navigation, kinematics, and control of the rover.

articleTitle: A Software Defined Radio for CCSDS 131.2-B protocol: exploiting Graphics Processing Unit accelerator for high performance data reception.
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: This paper presents the implementation of a Software Defined Radio receiver in compliance with the CCSDS 131.2-B standard. Such standard has been defined for all the missions which require high data rate transmissions, especially for Earth Observation missions, and makes use of Serially Concatenated Convolutional Code encoding. In this scope, the SDR receiver presented has been implemented, exploiting parallel processing, enhanced by the use of GPU, for dealing with the high data rate required by the CCSDS 131.2-B. The presented receiver represents a low-cost solution with respect to the State of The Art HW receivers.The paper gives an introduction about CCSDS 131.2-B standard and Graphics Processing Unit exposing the rationale for the implementation of a GPU-based SDR. Then the architecture of the receiver is described, focusing on the parallel computation that have been developed on GPU. Lastly the performance of the receiver are described in terms of data rate and bit error rate.

articleTitle: 64 Gbit Radiation Intelligent Memory Stack for Data Handling applications
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: The Radiation Tolerant Intelligent Memory Stack Flash (RTIMS FLASH) is a high density, user-friendly, off-the-shelf, radiation-protected NAND Flash memory.The memory module integrates a high-density NAND flash memory and a flash memory controller (FMC). The controller provides the module with full protection against SEL, SEFI and SEU. It also offers continuous logic sectors (no bad blocks) and high-value features such as wear leveling, memory self-test, internal registers for telemetry information. It is suitable as a small data recorder in space applications.

articleTitle: ADS SpE Fr High Efficiency, Versatile and Space Tolerant Point Of Load
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: This article presents Airbus DS Space Electronics France (ADS SpE) development of a versatile Point of Load, based on GaN technology, developed in the frame of the unified avionics initiative for Airbus Space Equipment Data Processing Units.

articleTitle: IngeniArs IP Cores for on-board high-speed data interfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: This paper describes how different IP Cores for on-board high-speed data interfaces have been developed and verified by IngeniArs S.r.l. These are the CODECs and Routers implementing SpaceWire and SpaceFibre communication protocols, i.e., the actual state-of-the-art for on-board data exchange in space applications. In addition, the WizardLink Front-End is presented.These IP Cores have not only been integrated into the space flight hardware of various European Space Agency missions, but have also been used for Electrical Ground Support Equipment (EGSE) implementation and in validation environments for other IP Cores, such as high-speed encoders and modulators.

articleTitle: Efficient In-Orbit CNN Updates
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: Building Artificial Intelligence (AI) models for Earth Observation (EO) satellites can be a difficult task since there is often no, or very limited, real training data available for a particular sensor. Even if data exists from a previous mission, a change in the sensor may make the model unsuitable. Therefore, being able to update the trained model, using the actual data provided by the sensor after the satellite is in orbit, is highly important. Thus, the main purpose of this work is to investigate and develop how to update remotely a model placed in a satellite in orbit, and how to control or specify the update size using the training parameters. The goal is to improve the accuracy performance of the model, using new data acquired from the in-orbit satellite, and to achieve this performance improvement under the criterion of reducing the size of the model update that is uplinked to the satellite. The method proposed selects which Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) layer weights must be modified and which must be fixed during training in order to maximize the accuracy increase and minimize the update file size. For a sample network, and without the proposed method, results show an update size of 44.5MB for the retrained network (with an original network size of 48.9MB), with retraining using the new data (such as that acquired from a satellite post-launch) resulting in an accuracy improvement from 78.4% to 79.9%. With the proposed Efficient Network Update (ENU) method, the generated post-training network update is only 18MB in size, but still achieves an accuracy of 78.9%. This demonstrates the reduced data bandwidth requirement to update the model, while gaining accuracy on the original trained network.

articleTitle: AI-based On-board Reconfigurable FDIR and Lifetime Prediction for Constellations
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: Constellations require complex operations and must grant high service availability. This makes autonomy and enhanced on-board Fault Detection, Isolation and Recovery (FDIR) one of the most urgent developments for the reduction of operational costs and of reaction times to events. This paper presents the results of an ongoing activity aiming at exploiting the assets available during satellites constellations development and operation, such as the models, the Avionics Test Bench, the operational data and events, to develop a workflow that allows fast implementation of high quality AI-based solutions for FDIR and lifetime prediction at constellation level. The ongoing activity benefits from the spin-in of diagnostics and prognostics solutions from similar automotive applications, characterised by combined on-board and off-board processing, operators-in-the-loop and need for on-board solutions easy re-configuration.

articleTitle: Current state and next generation of a systolic array SoC in space
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: The field of space applications has always been one of the most demanding and the challenges range from low power consumption to high performance data processing capabilities and from long component lifetime to remote control and flexibility. Engineers have to exploit each attribute the hardware provides and every particular requirement has to be coupled with an adequate design choice. The use of systolic arrays in a processing units brings to the arsenal of designers the possibility to have a very flexible and easily programmable solution, capable of performing parallelization of the most advanced and complex algorithms. After a brief description of the state-of-the-art HPDP chip and its multichip processing node, we will describe the next version of the device currently under design.

articleTitle: Hardware Accelerated Backprojection Algorithm on Xilinx UltraScale+ SoC-FPGA for On-Board SAR Image Formation
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: This paper describes the design and implementation of an HW/SW system to perform the computation of the Backprojection algorithm on an on-board Xilinx SoC-FPGA. It started with a hardware-agnostic high-level description of the algorithm in Matlab into a hardware-software system. In addition, the part of the algorithm mapped into the reconfigurable hardware was optimized to maximize the trade-off between image quality, performance, and required resources. The strategy of the optimization methodology consists of analysing the impact of custom wordlengths on all variables of the algorithm. Results show that it is possible to render a complete image of 501x501 pixels under 11.42s, which corresponds to a 2.43x speed-up when compared to the original software-only implementation.

articleTitle: The Universal Processing Module – Standardised Hardware for State of the Art Radar Data Conversion and Data Processing
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: The Universal Processing Module (UPM) is a sophisticated high speed digital hardware for spaceborne microwave applications incorporating in one single device most of the functionalities of the digital backend. The critical components of the UPM (ADCs, DACs, FPGA etc.) and their performance are the forefront of what is feasible for space as of today, hence UPM is a cutting-edge performance device. The customizable design of UPM itself, modular concept allowing performance extension by implementation of multiple modules and customization of the algorithms running on the device allow an application of UPM in multiple types of missions: from simple SAR payloads with classical performance up to sophisticated SAR Systems based on digital beamforming with a large number of digital channels. UPM is at a very advance development status and this paper describes the concept of the UPM, its key features and performance parameters.

articleTitle: SMOS-HR Correlator Architecture Processing Study
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: Within the framework of a phase A study for CNES of SMOS-HR (Soil Moisture and Ocean Salinity High Resolution) mission, Airbus Defence and Space has performed an architecture and feasibility study for the implementation of the correlator function. Due to the very large number of antennas and relatively large bandwidth, the processing power for the matrix correlation is massive with more than 7500 GMAC per second. An implementation in KU060 FPGA and VERSAL ACAP VC1902 has been performed and performance metrics have been analysed. For both implementations, bottlenecks have been identified and an optimised architecture proposed.

articleTitle: NimbleAI: 3D-Integrated Neuromorphic Vision Sensor-Processor to go where our Eyes can’t
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: AI paves the way for intelligent space agents that make autonomous decisions without the need for Earth-based interaction. Unfortunately, mainstream AI frameworks and algorithms as well as the COTS processors and AI accelerators on which these run are driven by the consumer market, and hence prioritize productivity over efficiency. The NimbleAI Horizon Europe project is aimed at redefining the basis of AI-based visual sensing and processing to boost efficiency by leveraging key biological principles in eyes and brains. The project will deliver novel neuromorphic hardware designs and IP to sustain event-driven vision with the following target KPIs: (1) 100x performance per mW gains compared to COTS processors (i.e., CPU/GPUs processing frame-based video); (2) 50x processing latency reduction compared to CPU/GPUs; (3) energy consumption in the order of tens of mWs; and (4) silicon area of approx. 50 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. This paper seeks liaison of the project with the space community and stakeholders to get feedback early in the design cycle, and ultimately increase adoption opportunities of NimbleAI technology in next-generation vision payloads.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Space-Grade FPGA Architectures
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: In this paper a comprehensive overview about State-of-the-Art Space-Grade FPGA and SoC-FPGA platforms from AMD, Microchip, NanoXlore and Frontgrade is presented. To this end, a resource-optimized LEON3 soft-core processor system is taken into account as a core design. For evaluation, resource utilization, achievable operating frequency, power consumption as well as radiation performance are taken into account. The results clearly point out the strengths and weaknesses of all space-grade FPGAs selected as well as it helps in the assessment and selection of the optimal candidate for upcoming space applications.

articleTitle: Vision Based Lunar Landing Using RC64 Rad Hard DSP/ML Manycore Processor
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: To enable Beresheet 2 Lunar landing, a real-time vision-based SLAM algorithm is executed on RC64, the rad-hard Space manycore, to simultaneously sense Lunar terrain and infer lander relative position, velocity, and attitude. Processing rate of 20 stereo 1024×1024 pixel images per second was achieved, consuming up to 6 Watts.

articleTitle: SpaceWire/SpaceFibre Analyser Real-Time (SpaceART) system extension to the Wizardlink Protocol
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: This paper presents an extension of the SpaceART EGSE to support the WizardLink protocol, a high-speed data transfer protocol for space applications. SpaceART is a real-time analyser and EGSE developed by IngeniArs, which supports SpaceWire and SpaceFibre protocols and can now also be used to test systems based on WizardLink protocol. WizardLink is a basic protocol defined by Texas Instruments and implemented in the TLK2711 chip, which provides several features that make it suitable for space applications, i.e., high-speed serial communication up to 2.5 Gbps, low power consumption, radiation tolerance and basic error detection.In this paper, the SpaceART WizardLink extension is presented, focusing on the description of its new features, Graphical User Interface and Application Programming Interface.A typical WizardLink scenario is presented as use-case for the usage of SpaceART WizardLink, involving the Payload Data Transmission section of an Earth Observation satellite. In this context, SpaceART WizardLink was used to implement an emulator for the Mass Memory.

articleTitle: On-Board Anomaly Detection on a Flight-Ready System
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: Within the scope of an ESA funded activity, Airbus Defence and Space GmbH completed a research and development study in order to provide a novel dataset to ESA and develop a flight-ready system for on-board anomaly detection. This work includes the extraction of satellite telemetry data, the identification of anomalies, the development of machine learning models and the flight-ready system and finally the deployment of the machine learning algorithms via hardware acceleration. We present the benchmarking results of three accelerated ML algorithms from within the final flight-ready system.

articleTitle: I. High Dependability Data Handling Systems for In Orbit Operations
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: Mars Sample Return program and others recent missions ask for some critical operations to be performed autonomously in orbit. Those operations are characterized by potentially catastrophic consequences in case of failure and the need for a high degree of autonomy. At DHS level, it is then necessary to provide a coverage of faults as extensive as possible and a reaction time as short as possible. This paper presents the DHS architecture proposed for two missions: MSR using traditional hardware and processes, in an institutional context, and a second one targeting a demonstration of docking in Low Earth Orbit. That later one with a strong bias toward the so-called new space. After a brief reminder of the aims of those missions a focus is made at both hardware and software level emphasizing the common concepts and differences. A conclusion is drawn for future programs with similar requirements.

articleTitle: Characterisation of RFSoC Gen 3 data converters for satellite RF payloads
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: This research paper presents a meticulous characterization of the integrated RF data converters—specifically, the RF-ADC and RF-DAC cores—in the Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+ RFSoC XCZU48DR device. The study was conducted using the ZCU208 evaluation board and adhered to IEEE standards for empirical analysis. The motivation for this research stems from the evolving requirements in satellite communications and microwave remote sensing, which necessitate a transition from traditional payload architectures to more flexible digital RF chains and Software-Defined Radios (SDRs). The paper provides empirical data on key performance metrics such as Effective Number of Bits (ENOB), Total Harmonic Distortion (THD), and Spur-Free Dynamic Range (SFDR) across a range of frequencies. The findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the capabilities and limitations of these data converters, thereby serving as a resource for future research and practical applications in advanced RF systems.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Space Applications Using RC64 Rad Hard Manycore Processor
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: Ramon.Space RC64 rad-hard manycore processor is designed for artificial intelligence/machine learning computations based on deep learning. VGG-based neural network classification of Space imagery of three different types is demonstrated. Machine learning models and imagery are provided by Aiko Space, Mobius Labs and Space Shift. Image frames of 32×32 pixels are classified at 65 frames per second, achieving power efficiency of 12.5 frames per second per Watt.

articleTitle: Modular Avionics Test Bench
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: This paper describes an ESA project that maps and tests interface and protocol compatibility of European cubesat/smallsat avionics-components. The project is called the Modular-Avionics-Test-Bench (MATB). The outcome is a modular-system that tests end-user requirements and interconnects various components.

articleTitle: A 22 nm 15 mW AI Accelerator to Enable On-Orbit Neural Network Inference for low-end CubeSats
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: A 6.4 GOPS/s AI accelerator with a power consumption of 15 mW is designed and fabricated. Its specifications enable real-time computer vision applications for low-end CubeSats. Software tooling to program the accelerator is also presented.

articleTitle: Radiation Test Results Demonstrating Operate-through Capability of an ESA Application Using Software Mitigation on a COTS GPU
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: The results of proton and total ionizing dose irradiation of a flight-proven onboard data processing unit are presented. Also, the efficacy of a software-based SEFI Mitigation Middleware was demonstrated via proton irradiation of the processor executing an ESA application.

articleTitle: Photonic Digital Data Handling at Airbus: From High End Definition to Component Technologies
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: In order to increase performances with higher data rate and benefit from a lower SWaP (Size, Weight & Power), photonic digital data handling is being implemented in replacement of copper harness. This paper aims to present different applications at Airbus using optical high speed serial links (HSSL) from telecom and earth observation payloads to platform data busses. Optical HSSL consists of an electro-optical (E/O) conversion to transmit the signal through optical fiber between different equipments followed by an O/E conversion. This leads to the implication of multiple partners as primes, equipment suppliers and also component industrials. Several technology solutions are available at component level allowing to meet the different challenges of primes (as complex routing with splitter box, integration…) and equipment suppliers (performance with suitable electro-optic transceiver but also compactness with optical flex). The present study investigates some of the most common elements and their impact on the architecture. From this, Airbus is leading compromises and choices to achieve standard technological solutions on the overall applications. The detail of the required developments on short, mid and long terms will be explored associated with the solution at prime and equipment supplier.

articleTitle: Challenges in the board implementation of VERSAL ACAP on a space board
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: The new generation of space grade component from AMD, the VERSAL ACAP, offers a significant increase in processing performance compared to current generation space grade FPGAs. The XQRVC1902 ACAP comes in a lidless 2197 pin BGA package with 0.92mm pitch. It can consume more than 100W, with a core voltage of 0.80V at currents up to more than 100A. The use of this component on a space qualified board brings many technical challenges. This paper will present some of those technical challenges and how Airbus Defence and Space is solving them.

articleTitle: CO2M Payload Data Handling Subsystem
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: Upcoming Space missions put new challenges in the domain of Space – Ground communication, in terms of higher downlink data rates & data volumes, and usage of less reliable communication links. These challenges, together with the goal to facilitate the Data Handling on Ground, pushed for the development and the usage of the File Based Operations (FBO) and protocols, like the CFDP, for automatic, selective retransmission of lost data. CO2M is the first Sentinels Mission to be launched, where the FBO and CFDP are implemented as per the Standards defined in the ESA Sentinel PUS-C Tailoring. Such protocols are used for the TC uplink, the Recorded HKTM downlink, and the Mission data downlink. The present paper deals with the consequent CO2M Satellite DHS peculiarities, in terms of architecture, data flow, and implemented Unit’s functionalities.

articleTitle: GRLIB: VHDL IP library for fault-tolerant SoC
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: GRLIB, a VHDL IP library developed and maintained by Frontgrade Gaisler, offers reusable VHDL IP cores that facilitate the development of system-on-chip designs. These cores, which include processors, memory controllers, bus infrastructure, and peripherals, support the creation of both simple controllers and complex system-on-chip designs with fault tolerance features. Designed to be flexible and easy to use, GRLIB is widely used in the space industry. It is vendor-independent, with built-in support for various EDA tools and target technologies. It also includes template designs for popular development boards from major vendors. The IP cores included have extensive heritage, reducing the time and effort required for design and verification, and ensuring reliable and high-quality systems.This digest offers an overview of GRLIB and highlights the latest additions to the library, the SPARC LEON5 processor, the RISC-V NOEL-V processor, a high-speed serial link controller supporting WizardLink and SpaceFibre, the GRSCRUB FPGA supervisor, a NAND Flash memory controller, and a DDR2/DDR3 memory controller with strong EDAC capabilities.

articleTitle: EDGX-1: A New Frontier in Onboard AI Computing with a Heterogeneous and Neuromorphic Design
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: In recent years, the demand for onboard artificial intelligence (AI) computing in satellites has increased dramatically, as it can enhance the autonomy, efficiency, and capabilities of space missions. However, current data processing units (DPUs) face significant challenges in handling complex AI algorithms and large datasets required for onboard processing. In this paper, we propose a novel heterogeneous DPU architecture that combines several different processing units into a single architecture. The proposed DPU leverages the strengths of each processing unit to achieve high performance, flexibility, and energy efficiency, while addressing the power, storage, bandwidth and environmental constraints of space. We present the design methodology for the DPU, including the hardware architecture and AI capabilities. The product represents a potentially significant advancement in the field of onboard AI computing in satellites, with applications in a wide range of space missions.

articleTitle: Mechanically Pumped Loop as Heatsink Solution for Advanced Onboard Data Processors
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: Advanced onboard processing comes with thermal challenges. This paper presents a solution to efficiently transport the dissipated power of a processor to a radiator. It is an active thermal control system that is capable of providing higher heat transport than the most efficient passive technologies -like heat pipes-, while keeping the added complexity low. The Mini-MPL system is a Mechanically Pumped Loop (MPL) solution intended for SmallSats that allows scalability in heat transport capability from 10 to 200 W and intended for a satellite quality class from CubeSat to MiniSat.

articleTitle: Testing Environment for TSN Deterministic Networking Based on Cots Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: This paper presents results of on-board networks where TSN protocols are deployed using different COTS switches. TSN performance was evaluated for different network topologies.

articleTitle: Payload Computer based on PolarFire SoC
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: The smart processing module (SPM) is an onboard computer for small satellites based on a Microchip PolarFire Flash System-on-Chip connected to several types of companion memories, such as MRAM, FRAM, and LPDDR. The SPM internal communication structure and related performance test results are presented. Furthermore, the results of a TID radiation test up to 11.7 krad are shown.

articleTitle: Design of an Edge Computing Space Board through the example of a Reference Design based on Quad ARM® Cortex®-A72 processing module
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: This document describes the steps, from components’ selection to their implementation, to design an Edge Computing Space Board, based on a Radiation Tolerant Quad Core ARM<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> Cortex<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> A-72 based processor and key Space grade components.

articleTitle: Panorama of Airbus Space Electronics processing products and technologies
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: Airbus Space Electronics France, part of the Space Products entity of Airbus Defence and Space (ADS), has decades of heritage in innovating and delivering high performance and high-quality space equipment for data handling and processing. This document presents an overview of Airbus Space Electronics France’s processing products and technologies.

articleTitle: Architecture Design of a High-Performance Mass Memory Unit based on Xilinx Versal FPGA for Future Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: Modern satellites carry increasingly complex and potent payload systems that produce valuable data for scientific or commercial purposes. These payloads generate high amounts of data in short timeframes which commonly exceeds the capacity of the available downlink channels. This, coupled with sparse contact windows to the ground station, necessitates a way to store payload data on-board for later transmission to ground. Therefore, mass memory units are key components of modern observation satellites. They provide the capability to store and retrieve payload data as well as housekeeping data generated on the satellite. In this paper the current status of a high-performance but reliable MMU development for next generation satellite systems based on a Microchip RTG4 and a Xilinx Versal FPGA is presented. The proposed design will reach data rates up to 20 Gbit s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−</sup>1 with a storage capacity of more than 48 Tbit. To this end the architectural design implementation details are shown.

articleTitle: The Radiative Transfer Equation inversion on FPGA. The case of the Photospheric Magnetic field Imager
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: We present the radiative transfer equation (RTE) inverter core, a high performance SIMD architecture, to interpret the data obtained by the Polarimetric and Magnetic field Imager (PMI) instrument aboard the ESA’s Vigil mission. After some pre-processing, the spectropolarimetric data will be translated on board into physical quantities of the solar atmosphere to be directly downloaded to Earth, hence strongly reducing the telemetry needs of such a deep space mission. The RTE inverter is direct heritage from that in the Polarimetric and Helioseismic Imager (PHI) aboard the ESA/NASA’s Solar Orbiter mission. The more stringent requirements of Vigil as compared to Solar Orbiter, as well as the production discontinuation of the FPGA used in the PHI instrument, have driven the migration of the inverter architecture to a brand-new, more powerful FPGA device (Xilinx Kintex UltraScale XQRKU060).

articleTitle: Insight4EO Architecture to Support Onboard AI Multiapplications from the End-User
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: Moving EO products onboard the spacecraft enables new scenarios of application. Data prioritization techniques can be applied to discard data without meaningful content to save bandwidth and power, or emergency management solutions can be employed to obtain timely alerts on ground even before the bulk data is available. However, the deployment of such solutions onboard the spacecraft presents two main challenges. First, EO products often require L1/L2 data that is not natively available onboard the spacecraft. Second, a suitable, easy to use, execution environment is needed to obtain the EO product with low latency. The Insight4EO solution presented here solves these two main problems by providing a L1/L2 product optimised to be run onboard the spacecraft for both SAR and optical payloads and a multiapplication processing enviroment based on Multi-Processor and FPGA.

articleTitle: GR765: SPARC and RISC-V Multiprocessor System-on-Chip
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: The GR765 is an octa-core system-on-chip that is currently in development and is being designed with high levels of radiation hardening and fault-tolerant features. This chip incorporates both the SPARC and RISC-V Instruction Set Architectures (ISA), providing users with the flexibility to choose the best architecture for their specific application requirements. The switching between the two ISAs is achieved through a bootstrap signal. The GR765 is designed with an advanced SoC architecture and a diverse set of peripherals, indicating its potential to serve as a robust and efficient computing platform.

articleTitle: Software Based Routing on Satellites - Redundant IP Packet Routing Architecture on Commercial Hardware with Traffic Prioritization
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: The growth of satellite constellations necessitates versatile data forwarding for IP packets. This paper proposes an architecture and an implementation of a redundant, space-grade, router architecture for IP packet routing based on Open vSwitch. The architecture is designed to be resilient against individual hardware failures and enables QoS routing capabilities as well as traffic prioritization. This approach permits IP routing on cost effective commercial hardware while retaining reliability.

articleTitle: DHS architecture for HERA Deep Space Mission
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: Deep Space missions must be autonomous and reliable systems, able to cope with no real-time communication with ground. Those systems shall be able to transmit to ground in reduce period of ground contact all data storage. For Hera satellite the DHS is defined to cope with those storage needs and the Spacewire network is defined to cope with real time packet transmission.

articleTitle: In Retrospect: Implementing a Custom SpaceWire Driver
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: This paper outlines our work to implement a custom SpaceWire driver for a deep space science mission. It discusses the reasons for choosing this approach over using a ready-made driver, the implementation costs and how sound this decision was in retrospect.

articleTitle: On-board Control Unit for ICE Cubes platform
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: This paper describes the design of an On-board Control Unit for space experiments conducted on ICE Cubes platform, hosted on Columbus module of the International Space Station. It provides an overview of the hardware and elaborates on two main aspects of the design: handling the experiments (power delivery and data acquisition) and providing Ethernet connectivity.

articleTitle: SmallSat payload Control and Data Processing unit
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: We have started the development of a new payload Control & Data Processing Unit (CDPU) targeted towards SmallSats. The CDPU will act as a hub for (optical) instruments that forms a logical bridge between the instruments and the SmallSat platform. It will offer standardized hardware interfaces for integrated optical instruments, as well as sophisticated facilities for processing the science data before it is sent down to earth. We defined a modular architecture to allow flexibility in interfaces and functions, with advanced and reliable in-orbit FPGA reprogrammability. The component quality class and applied development processes are chosen such to target for an in-orbit design lifetime in the order of 5 to 10 years.

articleTitle: An In-Depth Description of the Radiation Data Package for the QLS1046-Space Edge Processing Module
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: This document is detailing the complete Radiation Testing strategy performed on QLS1046-Space Edge Processing module, which is composed of a Quad Core ARM Cortex A72 and 4GB of high speed DDR4.

articleTitle: Efficient High Data Rate Networking Using Remote Direct Memory Access Over SpaceFibre
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: SpaceFibre [1] provides multi Gbit/s on-board networking for spaceflight applications. It has in-built quality-of-service (QoS); fault detection, isolation, and recovery (FDIR); and can run over electrical or fibre-optic cables. Using multiple lanes, it supports very high data rates. For example, with four lanes running at a lane signalling rate of 7.8125 Gbit/s, an overall link signalling rate of 31.25 Gbit/s is achieved. After adjusting for 8b/10b encoding and protocol overheads, this results in an approximate unidirectional data rate of 23.8 Gbit/s and bidirectional data rate of 23.1 Gbit/s.To support such high data rates in embedded systems with minimal processor overhead, this paper presents a SpaceFibre Endpoint that uses a Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) approach to provide zero-copy transferring of data between user-space applications over a SpaceFibre network.This paper first provides an overview of RDMA over SpaceFibre, then presents performance test results, and lastly describes an image transfer demonstration showing RDMA over SpaceFibre used in a real application.

articleTitle: GPU@SAT, the AI enabling ecosystem for on-board satellite applications
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: Today’s space missions perform increasingly complicated tasks on-board satellites, ranging from processing data to running artificial intelligence algorithms to enable new applications. As these algorithms have greater computational complexity, their execution may require dedicated hardware accelerators to provide timely results. This paper present GPU@SAT, a general-purpose GPU-like IP-core fitted on a radiation-hardened FPGA, with the purpose of enabling AI applications onboard satellite. The presented IP-Core is compatible with OpenCL 1.2 programming model, simplifying the development of computational intensive algorithms and their reusability. The design is highly parametrized, in order to adapt to different mission and platform requirements. Finally, a use case in which an AI algorithm will be deployed on GPU@SAT is presented, offering an interesting alternative to custom hardware accelerators.

articleTitle: GR740 Payload Controller Module - ADHA Compliant Next Generation Processing Module
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: The GR740 Payload Controller Module (GR740 PCM) currently in development at Airbus Crisa is based on the high-performance multi-core GR740 System-On-Chip (SoC) and the RTG4 reprogrammable FPGA which allow to provide a flexible HW architecture. This module is compatible with an ESA’s Advanced Data Handling Architecture (ADHA) System Slot for payload application while providing additional performances, maximizing the modularity and scalability of the product. The current development will result in an Engineering Model (EM) that will go through a complete HW characterization, including ambient thermal tests, leading to a TRL6 maturity level.

articleTitle: Hardware-Software co-design demonstrator for space applications on a Virtual Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: This document presents a hardware-software co-design demonstrator which is executed both in a Virtual Platform composed by SystemC/TLM models, and an actual COTS development board, with the objective of exhibiting the benefits of using such a flow for fast prototyping, early design space exploration decisions and co-engineering of software and hardware. Several enhancements are implemented in the Virtual Platform, and several use cases representative of potential space applications are executed in the demonstrator both in the Virtual Platform and on the actual hardware platform. The co-execution allows to compare the metrics obtained on the platform with the actual metrics obtained on the hardware, illustrating the usefulness of the HW-SW co-design approach.

articleTitle: Error Rate Estimation of DDR4-SDRAM Buffers in Space Mass Memories
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: DDR4-SDRAMs are key components widely used in modern computing systems on ground and in future space applications, where the sensitivity to ionizing radiation effects and the corresponding data integrity performance is of special interest. In this paper, an example DDR4-SDRAM buffer memory partition inside a high-performance mass memory system is described. For this buffer, two different EDAC implementations, which are Reed-Solomon single-symbol-error-correction and Reed-Solomon double-symbol-error-correction are compared in terms of data integrity performance. This comparison is based on the word error probabilities taking into account DDR4-SDRAM component specific single event effects and possible mitigation such as scrubbing and power cycling. The approach described in this work quantifies the design decision for a certain EDAC architecture as well as highlighting the impact of design parameters such as scrubbing and power cycling periods.

articleTitle: picoRTU-System: Distributed, Modular, Intelligent Remote Terminal Unit System
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: The main objective of the paper is to present a miniaturized distributed and intelligent remote terminal system, called picoRTU-system, based on modular off-the-shelf units for space applications, where each unit has its own set of user interfaces. Distributed RTU system is the first step to enable a truly distributed OBDH architecture with RTU functions closer to the data source.

articleTitle: Reference Implementations for Machine Learning Application Benchmark
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: This paper presents reference implementations for a multitude of space applications from the Machine Learning Application Benchmark. Reference implementations include the respective model, its on-board hardware implementation, test scripts and final benchmarking results. In publishing these reference implementations, we make a significant contribution to the benchmark and provide more insight into the viability of on-board machine learning applications.

articleTitle: A SpaceFibre Routing Switch for Distributed Payload Processing and Backplane Interconnect
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: SpaceFibre [1] is now operating in space and being designed into many more space missions. This paper considers a critical element in a SpaceFibre network, the routing switch, and describes an implementation which has been developed to technology readiness level (TRL) 5/6.

articleTitle: On-Board Processing for Communication Satellites – Principles and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: The increasing demand of communication services, coupled with rapidly changing customer needs lead to the introduction of more and more powerful On-Board Processors (OBP). The algorithmic and processing requirements for such an equipment are permanently increasing. Efficient use of limited spectral resources and the use of small terminals generally implies multi-beam satellite coverage and the associated need for digital beamforming and routing flexibility between beams favour on-board digital processing. Therefore it is time to face the challenges of this type of equipment.This paper provides a description of the advantages of the use of OBPs in telecommunications satellites, it describes the principles and challenges, and concludes with the work currently in progress.

articleTitle: Third Generation On Board Computer within the Advanced Data & Power Management System
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: In this paper, Redwire presents the selected Space On-Board Computer as part of our 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> generation ADPMS. Next to a general introduction of the features and its performance, we also clarify how our design is flexible and can handle a wide range of mission and system challenges.

articleTitle: Application of AMD Versal™ Adaptive SoC to Radar Space Time Adaptive Processing in Space
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: Space Time Adaptive Processing (STAP) radar systems require rapid execution of complex matrix multiplications to calculate and apply covariances and adaptive filtering weights, to achieve filtering of ground clutter and to mitigate jamming. Developers of these systems require capabilities to rapidly simulate and prototype their designs. In this paper we discuss the signal processing requirements of a modern STAP radar system, and describe the implementation of a STAP design in two phases – firstly with a hardware-in-the-loop simulation using MATLAB<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> and Simulink<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> from MathWorks<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> and an AMD Versal™ Adaptive SoC, and secondly with a full implementation in the AMD Versal Adaptive SoC, which is available as a radiation-tolerant space-grade device. Our two implementation phases make use of the Adaptive Intelligent Engines in the Versal architecture to achieve rapid execution of matrix multiplication with complex values and to allow rapid modification of algorithms, without incurring additional development time due to repeated place-and-route and static timing analysis cycles.

articleTitle: Standardization concepts for CubeSat applications
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: Due to physical/power/financial constraints of CubeSats, classical improvements of reliability in area of satellite avionics and data-handling (i.e. redundant subsystems, cross-strapping) are not usually possible. On top of that, CubeSat development rarely follows technical standards, and is usually based on COTS solutions additionally questioning reliability figures.This article proposes the use of concepts implemented usually on "bigger" satellites migrated into the world of CubeSat applications. Those concepts are described in SAVOIR working group, which standardises certain data-handling functionalities expected to be present in "mature" satellite. By applying specific engineering solutions and guidelines, most of the SAVOIR functions can be implemented in CubeSat, therefore increasing the reliability.

articleTitle: New Space Challenges: Unique Scalable Solutions
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: New Space challenges drive semiconductors and space industry to look to more scalability and trade-offs according to the targeted mission. Reuse from other domains is also key to reduce costs and time to market. With Unique Scalable solutions inherited from Automotive, Microchip France pave the way towards new capabilities and system use cases.

articleTitle: Advanced Data Handling Architecture (ADHA): On-board Computer (OBC) Module
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: The ADHA (Advanced Data Handling Architecture) program is an initiative of the European Space Agency (ESA) in collaboration with European industrial partners for the development of a standardized, modular and scalable platform for data handling and data processing systems, based on inter-operable and interchangeable electronic modules. One of the main constituent parts of an ADHA unit is the On-Board Computer (OBC) module which, along with the standard OBC functions of a satellite, it also implements the role of a System Controller within the ADHA unit. This paper will present an overview of the specifications, functional and software architectures, ADHA unit configurations and the role of the OBC module within an ADHA system.

articleTitle: XSWITCH-16: Rad-Hard Crosspoint Switch IC for High-Speed Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: This paper presents design considerations of XSWITCH-16, a radiation hardened 16x16 full duplex Crosspoint Switch integrated circuit (IC) offering repeater, multiplexer, and switch functions capable of reaching bit rate as high as 12 Gbps thanks to the digital re-timing architecture. Overall presentation of circuit architecture and brief presentation different functions are discussed. (Abstract)

articleTitle: An overview of the electrical, electronic and on-board data handling architecture of the Ariel Payload
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: Ariel, the Atmospheric Remote-sensing Infrared Exoplanet Large-survey mission [1], [2], has been selected by ESA in March 2018 and adopted in November 2020 by the Agency for the fourth medium-class mission (M4) launch opportunity of the Cosmic Vision Program, scheduled in 2029. It is the first survey mission dedicated to measuring the chemical composition and thermal structures of the atmospheres of hundreds of transiting exoplanets, in order to enable planetary science far beyond the boundaries of our own Solar System. The Payload (P/L) and its electrical, electronic and data handling architecture, scope of this digest, has been designed and optimized to perform transit spectroscopy from space during primary and secondary planetary eclipses in order to achieve a large set of unbiased observations related to the nature of exoplanets atmospheres, retrieving information about planets interior and determining the key factors affecting the formation and evolution of planetary systems.

articleTitle: SpaceWire Based Reconfiguration and Redundancy Management of COTS Based Highly Integrated Onboard Computer
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: This paper proposes a dynamic reconfiguration and redundancy solution for a next generation of COTS based Highly Integrated Computer System (CHICS) based on Xilinx Multiple Processor System on Chip (MPSoC) acting as a processor and Polarfire Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) acting as a supervisor using purely Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) components. The proposed architecture uses warm redundancy with dual lanes, nominal and redundant, each lane comprising of a processor and a supervisor. They are interconnected via SpaceWire on a compact PCI back plane making a CHICS pair. In each lane, the supervisor is responsible for monitoring the system and performing reconfiguration in case of a failure. Additionally, we have the option of switching between the nominal and redundant lanes seamlessly in case of a critical fault. The proposed solution is robust, efficient, and cost-effective, making it suitable for use in space applications targeting missions for Low Earth Orbits (LEO). In this paper we present the algorithm for reconfiguration along with the redundancy switchover and discuss the metrics obtained during the reconfiguration process.

articleTitle: The Olympe Demonstrator
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: The Olympe project aims to assess the performances offered by the NG-Ultra device and its suitability for future applications such as Platform On-Board Computer. This article presents this project, the test set, the test scope, and technical outcomes so far with an emphasis on performance, boot strategy, and hardware implementation as a cPCI-Serial-Space module (anticipating ESA’s Advanced Data Handling Architecture (ADHA) standard).

articleTitle: Intelligent Space Camera for On-Orbit AI-Driven Visual Monitoring Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: The Intelligent Space Camera (ISC) is a compact space camera with embedded Computer Vision and Artificial Intelligence capabilities, that can address applications requiring high-throughput smart processing directly at source. The camera, incorporating both hardware and software elements, is being developed in the frame of an ESA co-funded project to support space situational awareness, visual FDIR, and docking applications, among others. The camera, built around the Myriad X Vision Processing Unit (VPU), supports RTSP streaming, H.265 encoding, dynamic remote reconfiguration, and in-line AI stream processing at framerate, all directly on-camera. Processing results can be sent to the host as metadata or overlaid on the RTSP stream (e.g., as bounding boxes). This paper describes the system in its current form from a software and hardware point of view, as well as its key features and main use cases.

articleTitle: Enhanced Computational Storage Device Employing AI-based Triage
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: The popularity of Artificial Intelligence (AI) applications is counterbalanced by their cost in terms of time and energy. Traditional computing systems have evolved with separate computing and storage units, which require data movement in order to perform data processing. Computational Storage Device (CSD) technologies have been proposed in order to push data processing to the data in order to reduce time consumption, memory, energy, and bandwidth usage. In this paper, an Enhanced CSD (3CSD) will be introduced. An efficient and flexible storage device-based triage, that provides a seamless workflow to process and infer data in place represents an evolution in terms of traditional CSD which employs a store-first inference-later paradigm. The experimental results show that the purpose of Multistage LILLIAN (LeveragIng Last-miLe data usIng context-based AutolabelliNg) increases the performance of the triage detectors by 20%. Furthermore, some state-of-the-art fusion approaches are evaluated including late fusion (Ensembles) which boosted the performance of the triage subsystem significantly. Experimental results are evaluated using Intel Movidius MyriadX.

articleTitle: Multi-Purpose COTS-based Edge AI Computing Platform for Small Satellite Mission Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: This work covers the design of an edge AI computing platform targeting CubeSats, based on commercial off-the-shelf components, developed jointly by AAC Hyperion and the Royal Netherlands Aerospace Centre (NLR). We present the architectural design of the unit from both a software and a hardware perspective as well as the TID/SEE testing campaign results. Capabilities for future developments using the proposed design as a foundation are also discussed.

articleTitle: Advanced Data Handling Architecture (ADHA): System Architecture and Design Description
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: The present paper is intended to provide a report of the ADHA Consolidation, Standardization, and Product Suite Development technical status. Since this project is currently under execution, the reported results correspond to the status at the Preliminary Design Review (performed between June and September 2023).

articleTitle: Self-Calibrating Electronic Controller for Satellite Quantum Entanglement Source
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: Due to the rapid growth of interest related to Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) for secure communication applications, the importance of entangled photon source control and read-out electronics increases. In most cases dedicated laboratory equipment are used to generate, collect and store Quantum Keys for encryption purposes. Reliable and effective quantum key generation at long distances requires an entangled photon pair generator, which is a precise optical device requiring alignment and calibration. Calibration can be performed on the ground before a flight, as well as in-orbit, during a flight. In many cases, this process needs to be performed periodically – once a month or even once a week. An approach with calibration on the ground requires a more sophisticated mechanical design that prevents the decalibration. However, in many cases preventing the decalibration by the mechanical design might not be possible. This paper shows the results of development in the scope of hardware, Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGA) and software under Self-Calibrating Electronic Controller for Satellite Quantum Entanglement Source (SECSQES) project.

articleTitle: A novel multi-mission platform for the development of applications, services, and new satellite data algorithms directly in orbit and on-demand, the Italian In-Orbit Space Lab
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: In several vertical industries where Earth Observation (EO) data are used today (e.g., agriculture, resource management, etc.), users are focused on their core application, less interested in the data itself and more in the tools that can make their business more efficient and effective. In some contexts (e.g., fire detection) the right information needs to be provided to end users (or potential customers of a service) at the right time and in the right place. And the right place can be in some cases the space segment, where the availability of usable information can be a tipping point. In this approach, part of the EO value chain is shifted from the ground segment to the space segment, to transform sensed data into" intelligence" in a timely manner, to exploit it directly or to enable the optimized exploitation of limited on-board resources (in fire detection this means the downlink of the alert alone with its geographic location, a few dozen bytes instead of GB of raw data). This is the path to transform EO into" Earth Intelligence.". However, such a transition still has inefficiencies that can reduce mission effectiveness and increase operational costs, and most importantly lengthen development time along the entire value chain, from the implementation of new sensors to the testing of innovative algorithms on orbit. In this rapidly changing scenario, training and incubation processes need to be adapted to the new reality, breaking down barriers and mitigating mortality risks for new ventures: this is why the development of a dedicated infrastructure, consisting of a Space and Ground Segment, enabling the realization of a hybrid cloud system that makes data, sensors, AI\cognitive capabilities available, on-demand, in the cloud on the ground and in orbit, at the edge in a federated manner

articleTitle: Flight hardware optimisation through modularity and building blocks
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: This paper presents the advantages and technical difficulties of the development of a modular architecture. It shows the impact of standardisation on process development, qualification and industrial aspects.

articleTitle: Amethyst constellation OBC mass production
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: In contrast to the traditional satellite industry based on missions made up of one or few identical satellites, building hundreds of satellites for large constellations requires innovation and the implementation of radical changes in the design, manufacturing and assembly of the satellites and their components. The OneWeb constellation is made up of 648 satellites to provide affordable internet worldwide with 542 satellites launched as of January 2023. In light of the development and deployment of this constellation, and more particularly in light of the first On-Board-Computer developed by Airbus dedicated to large constellations, named Amethyst, this digest is addressing the way the space industry has adapted to these recent major evolutions., Additionally, this digest paper will address the new and upcoming challenges.

articleTitle: A Practical Framework to Specify the Prototype Filters for the Analysis of Frequency Stacked Sub-bands
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: Frequency stacking in the analog domain is used to replace multiple narrowband ADCs with a wideband ADC, supporting multiple antenna elements for digital satellite beamforming. This analog front end provides a cost-effective solution by offering a common broadband digital interface to the onboard processor, which can be configured for multiple satellite missions. This paper is on specifying the prototype filters to analyse frequency-stacked mobile sub-bands in the digital domain. The paper further presents results and observations that demonstrates the effectiveness of this specification for a given mobile narrowband communication scenario. Index Terms—Satellite Communication Systems, Digital Signal Processing, Analog-to-Digital Convertor.

articleTitle: A Synthetic Image Data Generation Pipeline for Spacecraft Fly-by Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: Accessible, high-quality datasets for machine learning activities remain limited to this date. Especially for space applications, this is relevant, but even more difficult is it for exploration missions, where the data to be obtained is not known beforehand. To reduce this lack of data, this work proposes a pipeline for automatic realistic data generation for fly-by scenarios such as planned for ESA’s Comet Interceptor mission. The pipeline consists of two components. First, creating digital models of the nucleus and dust cloud using Blender and second, adding camera artefacts with Python. The camera artefacts considered here are radiation effects, image fractures, pixel errors, thermal noise, and dark current. The goal of the pipeline is to generate realistic data with camera artefacts to supplement the limited available real image footage. Additionally, the synthetic generation of data with random combinations of factors will allow to cover many possible scenarios, for example, irregular body shapes like was observed during ESA’s Rosetta mission. The generated data will be used to train efficient neural networks to be deployed on-board spacecrafts’ future processing systems which enable increased data reduction capabilities in space. The pipeline is also designed to create data to verify the system’s behaviour in certain scenarios.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence for Earth Observation
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: Let’s imagine new EO satellite use cases and how they could be put into shape.

articleTitle: Redundant imaging payload data processing system based on a heterogeneous MPSoC
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: We present a payload data processing unit for imaging payloads in New Space earth observation missions. The system is based on a commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) heterogeneous multiprocessing System-on-a-Chip (MPSoC). To increase the reliability beyond what is possible using only software mitigation techniques, a dual cold redundant configuration is chosen.

articleTitle: On Board Data Analysis and Realtime Information System
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: For many information applications like alarming services or surveillance systems, reactivity is a very important criterion. This is also true for many applications based on satellite data, for example in the field of remote sensing or space system operation. These applications are currently bottlenecked by classical satellite operation, where contact to the satellite is only established within a few communication windows, when the satellite is in reach of an assigned ground station. The amount of time between collection of the data on the space system and having it available for ground-users can take from several hours up to days.At our institution, we are working on a cost-efficient method to decrease the latency until information, derived from satellite data, becomes available for usage on ground. The basic approach is trying to utilizing satellite based low-latency real-time telecommunication networks, designed for ground-based satellite phone usage in combination with on board information extraction. Information extraction on the satellite will be necessary as the telecommunication networks only offer a very limited data-transfer bandwidth in the range of a few hundred bytes and the transmission of raw sensor data is not possible.

articleTitle: In-Orbit Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning On-Board Processing Solutions for Space Applications : Edge-Based and Versal Space Reference Designs : First Design-In Experiences
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: An increasing number of on-board processing applications require intelligent, real-time in-orbit processing to extract value-added insights, rather than clog precious RF downlinks with bandwidths of data for cloud-based, post-processing on the ground. Some applications require autonomous, immediate decision making, e.g. a LEO spacedebris retrieval spacecraft outside of its ground-station contact time would not be able to receive a late command to initiate a collision-avoidance maneuver, or a defense satellite performing space domain awareness using data from multiple sensors followed by object detection and classification may require a friend or foe decision. High-definition SAR imagery is increasingly generating huge amounts of Earth-observation data and in-orbit AI inference and the implementation of neural networks allows for feature identification and characterization to assist real-time decision-making, e.g. tracking wildfires or floods.

articleTitle: Performance and Radiation Testing of the Coral TPU Co-processor for AI Onboard Satellites
publicationTitle: 2023 European Data Handling & Data Processing Conference (EDHPC)
abstract: COTS HW and SW components become crucial for advancing AI in space applications. The CAIRS21 ESA project considers Coral TPU as a candidate AI co-processor in avionics and examines its suitability in terms of performance, programmability/productivity, and radiation tolerance.
